To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pre-training GNNs is a promising approach to improve the generalization of GNNs; (2) naïve strategies, such as pre-training at the level of graphs or individual nodes separately, can even lead to a negative transfer; (3) our proposed strategy, which pre-trains GNNs at both levels simultaneously, is effective in avoiding negative transfer and improving generalization significantly across different downstream tasks.

(1) pre-training GNNs at individual node level and graph level can improve the performance on downstream tasks; (2) the performance of pre-training GNN is highly dataset dependent; (3) the pre-trained GNN model is more robust than a non-pre-trained one.

(1) Pre-training Graph Neural Nets is a promising approach to improve generalization, (2) Pre-training at the graph level is necessary to learn useful graph-level representations, but it is insufficient to learn useful node-level representations, and (3) Pre-training at both the node and graph levels is necessary to improve generalization on downstream tasks
